title: A command dispatcher
description:
Read commands from standard input and dispatch them through a table of functions.

```
> add 3 4
7
> mul 6 7
42
> neg 5
-5
> fly 1 2
unknown command
```

starter.main.asm:
global  _start

        section .bss
line:   resb    128

        section .text
_start:
        lea     rdi, [rel line]
        mov     esi, 128
        call    read_line
        mov     rdi, rax
        call    print_int
        call    print_newline
        mov     eax, 60
        xor     edi, edi
        syscall

hints: Store each table entry as two `dq`s: the address of the name and the address of the function (lesson 8.03).
Split the line at spaces by replacing them with zero bytes, keeping pointers to each part.
requirements: A table of `(name, function)` pairs: names as zero-terminated strings, functions as addresses.
Look the command name up by comparing strings, then `call` through the register.
Numbers parsed with your own routine; bad input prints a message instead of crashing.
stretch: Add `help`, which prints every name in the table.
